transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this review session. As you know, a student who is below the college's academic-standing standard must receive a written academic recovery contract for the spring term, and the student has submitted a draft plan asking to return to regular enrollment after the spring term. Before I approve and sign the final contract, I need to gather the information each of you can provide. Let's go through the required components: the student's enrollment plan, any conditions for continued enrollment, and the support services that will be monitored. I'd like to hear from each of you in turn. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to start. During my advising review, I found an important issue with the draft plan. My degree audit shows that the student's only approved way to repair the failed major requirement this term is to repeat CHEM 201, a 4-credit course. However, the draft plan currently lists a different elective instead. This mismatch needs to be corrected before the contract is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to add an important condition that needs to be written into the contract. I've verified in the registrar's standing rule that the student's academic-standing reinstatement requires 12 completed credits during the spring term — not merely enrollment in an unspecified full-time load. This specific condition has not yet been entered into the contract template, and it needs to be included before Dr. Morgan signs off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have information relevant to the enrollment conditions. In my counseling session with the student, I confirmed that the student has a documented caregiving obligation. This makes a 12-credit load manageable only if at least 6 of those credits are delivered asynchronously. I recorded this in my counseling file, but I have not yet sent this delivery condition to the dean. I believe this asynchronous-credit condition should be written into the contract before Dr. Morgan signs off.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a critical financial-aid condition that must be written into the contract. I've confirmed that the student's financial-aid appeal remains eligible only if the recovery contract requires advisor meetings every two weeks for the first 8 weeks of the term. I received this condition from the aid committee, but I have not yet attached it to the academic contract. This condition needs to be included before Dr. Morgan signs off, or the student's financial-aid appeal will lose eligibility.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: The contract will be corrected to list CHEM 201 (4 credits) instead of the elective currently in the draft plan.
The contract will include the condition that the student must complete 12 credits during the spring term for academic-standing reinstatement.
The contract will include the condition that at least 6 of the 12 credits must be delivered asynchronously, as documented in the counseling file.
The contract will include the condition that the student must attend advisor meetings every two weeks for the first 8 weeks of the term to maintain financial-aid appeal eligibility.

transcript.speaker: A1
